title: Minimal Impact From Fed
summary:
Minimal Impact From Fed 

             
             
            Fed day has come and gone with minimal fanfare. Markets ultimately found reason to downgrade expectations for future rate hikes (likely due to Warsh's general "wait and see" comments during the press conference), but at the expense of a bit of weakness in the longer end of the yield curve. In other words, 2yr yields fell and 10yr yields rose. Neither were appreciably far from levels seen 2 days ago.  Additionally, not all of the above should be attributed to the Fed. 10yr yields are actually ending the day lower compared to levels seen around noon (2 hours before the Fed announcement). Overnight weakness in the 10yr is easier to connect to lower funding costs for some of the neocloud companies that have recently been under the microscope. Afternoon gains corresponded with Oracle saying it anticipated lower funding needs.

title: Mortgage Rates Move Modestly Higher
summary: Today's Fed announcement had no impact on mortgage rate movement, and minimal impact on intraday bond market volatility. Well before the Fed announcement, the bond market was already slightly weaker compared to yesterday's latest levels. As a result the average mortgage lender set rates just a hair higher.  Despite the increase, 30yr fixed rates are only 0.05% above the low of 7.30% seen last week and only 0.02% above yesterday's mark of 7.33%. Recent upward pressure is a factor of improvement in investor sentiment surrounding the tech sector.

title: AI Governance, License Renewal, Servicing Transfer, SOC Products; Fannie Earnings
summary: The other day I went to Costco, and for $5.99 bought a pumpkin pie the size of a hubcap. What inflation? Costco’s hot dog/soda combo or the rotisserie chicken are loss leaders, but actual gasoline, beef, lettuce, restaurant meals, goods from overseas, and other items’ price changes have kept inflation in the headlines and impacted mortgage rates. (Other headlines include Fannie Mae earning $4.2 billion in the 3rd quarter; more below.) What about water prices and availability… are they important to homeowners or potential buyers? What happens when you combine something like clean water with a private supplier? How about “a problem.” I am not saying that this is similar to private companies investing in mortgage-backed securities, but in the Navaho Nation, mostly in Northeast Arizona, a large percentage of residents don’t even have running water. Hawai’i was hit with a hurricane which has shut down water service on the Big Island. One community’s water and sewer needs are served by a utility that is not insured, has no money secured for repairs, and no timeline for restoring service. title: USDA Fast-Track Mortgage Pilot Doubles In Size
summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture is doubling the number of lenders in a pilot program designed to speed up rural mortgage closings.Six additional lenders will join USDA's Delegated Authority Lender Interactive Test Environment (LITE) Pilot Program on Dec. 1, bringing the total number of selected participants to 12.The latest additions are Bangor Savings Bank, Fairway Independent Mortgage Corp., New American Funding, Pennymac Loan Services, Pulte Mortgage, and Union Home Mortgage.

title: Nearly Half Of Foreclosures Involve Newer Loans As FHA Auctions Surge
summary: Mortgages originated since 2022 now account for nearly half of completed foreclosure sales, while foreclosure auction activity involving those newer loans has surged 73% over the past year, according to separate reports from Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) and Auction.com.The findings point to a significant shift in the foreclosure pipeline, with loans originated during the higher-rate, higher-home-price environment increasingly appearing among distressed properties.

title: The Home Equity Paradox Facing Divorcing Homeowners
summary: For most homeowners, rising property values are good news. But during a divorce, years of appreciation can create an unexpected problem: The more equity a couple has accumulated, the harder it may be for one spouse to afford to keep the home.A property that once represented shared financial security can suddenly require a six-figure payout. And the spouse who wants to stay must often finance that obligation on a single income, potentially replacing a low-rate mortgage with a much larger loan at today's rates.

title: Zillow Covers FHA Down Payments, Steps Up Competition For Purchase Loans
summary: Zillow Home Loans is offering to cover the entire minimum down payment for eligible FHA borrowers, adding a new financing incentive to its growing mortgage business and raising the competitive stakes for independent loan originators.The program, announced Wednesday, provides up to 3.5% of the purchase price or appraised value, whichever is lower, through a second mortgage with no interest or monthly payment. The loan is forgiven after five years if the borrower makes on-time payments on the primary mortgage and continues occupying the home.

title: Homeowners Are Delaying Repairs. Lenders Could Face The Consequences.
summary: More than one-third of U.S. homeowners have postponed needed repairs or maintenance over the past two years, according to a new LendingTree survey, and some are finding that waiting only makes the problems worse.Among homeowners with outstanding repairs, 34% say delays have increased costs, 29% report that the original problem has worsened, and 25% say the delays have caused damage elsewhere in their homes.
